subject: EdgePack GCP marketplace: anchoring proposal + reseller offset request
messages:
From: Peter Huang <peter@edgepack.io>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: procure@edgepack.io
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 09:07:12 -0700
Subject: GCP marketplace private offer - anchor price and reseller offsets

Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo last week. EdgePack is close to finalizing a purchase path via GCP Marketplace and we wanted to explore a private offer construct that matches our procurement workflows. Two asks up front: (1) can Redwood anchor list price on the GCP listing instead of the higher committed private offer list so our USD budgeting aligns with internal systems, and (2) we need a clear reseller offset (EdgePack sells through two channel partners) so we can model margins for our channel finance team.

Attached is a short usage forecast and a strawman pricing sheet (edgepack-pricing-v2.xlsx). Our preferred timeline is closing the PO and private offer sign-off by mid-Oct.

Key constraints on our side: multi-year commitment runs across two cloud regions (us-west and us-east), and our procurement requires the marketplace listing to show the public list price for audit. We understand private offers can include committed discounts but want the visible SKU to be stable.

Could your team confirm whether Redwood can:
- Set the public listing anchor at the sticky list price (we would still accept a private-offer-only discounted commit)
- Allow a 6% reseller offset to be passed to our local partner without breaking marketplace billing reconciliation
- Provide a short SOW template that maps usage tiers to committed discounts (SOW attached)

If helpful, I can loop in our cloud marketplace ops lead.

Thanks,
Peter
VP, Partnerships
EdgePack

Hi Peter — great to hear you're progressing. Appreciate the forecast and SOW. High-level responses below; Ben and Irene are cc'd to confirm operational and channel policy feasibility.

Short answers:
- Public listing anchor: we can publish a stable list price on the Marketplace listing and deliver the private offer as a separate committed discount. That keeps your procurement/audit flows intact.
- Reseller offset: we often support pass-through offsets to partners but need to validate the exact accounting path with Finance; 6% sounds reasonable as long as it is modeled as a reseller credit and not an invoice line item that changes marketplace grossing.
- SOW mapping: thanks for the SOW — I'll have our solutions template back to you with modest edits for tiering clarity.

Next steps I propose:
1) Ben to confirm channel/pass-through mechanics (invoice routing & bookkeeping).
2) Irene to confirm private offer packaging (SKU anchoring + committed tiers) and any restrictions across regions.
3) Quick call Thurs 09/31 or Friday to align the procurement/legal ask.

We're aligned to target mid-Oct. Thanks, and will follow up after Ben/Irene weigh in.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Account Exec, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: GCP marketplace private offer - anchor price and reseller offsets

Lauren / Irene — I dug into how we can handle the 6% reseller offset from an ops and finance perspective. Notes: 

- We can support a reseller credit via a passback flow: Redwood issues monthly credits to EdgePack's partner account tied to usage reconciliation. That preserves marketplace invoicing (GCP still invoices end customer at net-of-private-offer price).
- Legal/Tax: we need procurement to sign an annex acknowledging the offset flow (so we don't treat the offset as a deduction in Redwood's recognized revenue without proper reseller agreements). I've attached a short clause suggestion in the pricing sheet.
- Accounting hit: credits will be recorded as contra-revenue on Redwood side; we should capture the approval under RDW-EDGE-2026-089 for rev rec audit.
- Ops constraint: cross-region buckets are fine but private offers are regional; we'll need separate offer entries for us-west and us-east with the same anchor but mirrored SKUs. This is painless but will add a small ops lead-time (2–3 business days).

Ask: Irene, can you confirm we can publish identical list prices on both regional listings while creating two private offers that point to the same commitment schedule? Also: legal will want to see the draft annex before final sign-off.

Thanks — tagging finance and legal in the next thread if we get verbal go-ahead.

Ben
Head of Deal Ops, Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>

Thanks all — confirming operational feasibility and a recommended playbook: 

1) Anchor/list price: we will publish the anchor SKU at the agreed list price in both us-west and us-east listings. Private offers will be created per region and scoped to the commit tiers you provided.

2) Reseller offset: approved at 6% as a monthly credit to the partner account. Legal will require an Annex A that spells out the credit computation and reconciliation cadence (monthly usage reconciliation, 30-day dispute window). I'll draft the Annex and share by EOD Monday.

3) Deal packaging: create two private offers (one per region) referencing the same commitment ID RDW-EDGE-2026-089. The offer documents will include: commit tiers, overage rates, listed anchor SKU, and the reseller-offset clause.

4) Timeline: ops can stand up both offers within 48 hours of legal acceptance of the annex. Finance: Ben, please confirm the revenue treatment note and the internal code for the credit so we can tag it at creation time.

Lauren — I'll join the call Friday to run through the annex and SOW edits. Peter — once legal signs off we'll send a DocuSign link for the annex + private offer acceptance.

Best,
Irene Choi
Director, Marketplace & Partnerships
Redwood Inference
